newsitem.title: USA: Israel's U.S. envoy hits Arafat "blackmail".
newsitem.headline: Israel's U.S. envoy hits Arafat "blackmail".

text.p: Israel's envoy to Washington on Saturday accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of trying to "blackmail" Israel into halting work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem by condoning violence against Israel.

Ambassador Eliahu Ben-Elissar told CNN Arafat also released hundreds of activists from the Moslem extremist group Hamas just days before Friday's suicide bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe that killed three Israeli women.

Hamas claimed responsibility for the attack and threatened on Saturday to launch further attacks if Israel continued build 6,500 homes for Jews on a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, a project Arafat and other Palestinian leaders have repeatedly urged halted.
Fierce Israeli-Arab clashes flared in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday for the second straight day.

"If we are in disagreement, there is only one way to solve those disagreements -- by negotiating, not by terror," Ben-Elissar said. "The demonstrations ... in Hebron are not spontaneous, they have been orchestrated."
Anger about the Israeli settlements should have been controlled by Arafat's Palestinian Authority, he said, adding, "but they simply gave a nod to this ...criminal activity."
"This is blackmail behaviour," Ben-Elissar said. "They are simply putting a gun to our forehead."
He denied that construction of the Israeli settlement had anything to do with the peace process, and said any Israeli work in Jerusalem was likely to prompt an emotional response.
Nesser Al-Kidwa, Palestinian representative to the United Nations, also speaking on CNN, denied Ben-Elissar's allegations and said they were "irresponsible."

"It's a matter of policy and also common sense that these things hurt our cause and we would never condone or encourage something like that," Al-Kidwa said, suggesting that Israeli words and actions in recent weeks appeared designed to derail the peace process.
"On our side we are commiteed to the process, committed to the agreement, and we want to go further," he said.
Al-Kidwa denied the violence in Hebron was orchestrated and said he viewed Ben-Elissar's suggestion that it was as "condescending" toward its partners in the peace process.
